lists.content:
Strategic Leadership & Ownership

  • Define and execute the QA strategy across all Xsolla products, aligning quality objectives with business goals and product roadmaps.

  • Own QA deliverables end-to-end - from test planning through release sign-off - and be accountable for outcomes, not just activities.

  • Establish and enforce quality gates, defect governance policies, and release readiness criteria across all product teams.

  • Drive organizational maturity: evolve the QA function from reactive testing to proactive quality engineering embedded in every stage of the SDLC.

  • Represent QA at the executive level - articulate quality risks, tradeoffs, and resource needs to VP/C-level stakeholders with clarity and data.


    • Technical Excellence

    • Architect and oversee enterprise-grade test automation frameworks spanning UI (Playwright), API, database validation (SQL), and performance testing (K6).

    • Define and maintain standards for test code quality - including code reviews, PR contributions, reusable libraries, and modular test design.

    • Deep understanding of Git workflows - branching strategies, merge request reviews, repository hygiene, and code versioning best practices across multiple repositories.

    • Expert-level knowledge of CI/CD pipelines - design, optimize, and troubleshoot automated build, test, and deployment pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar).

    • Ensure all automation is fully integrated into CI/CD pipelines, with clear pass/fail signals, automated regression gates, and performance benchmarks at every release stage.

    • Drive adoption of infrastructure-as-code practices for test environments - containerized test execution, ephemeral environments, and environment parity between staging and production.

    • Evaluate, select, and implement QA tooling - including test management platforms (Qase), observability tools, and defect tracking integrations.


      • AI Integration & Innovation

      • Proven track record of using AI in day-to-day QA activities - not aspirational, but demonstrated. You have used AI tools to generate test cases, write automation code, analyze test results, identify flaky tests, or accelerate debugging.

      • Champion and operationalize AI-assisted quality engineering across the organization - specifically using Claude AI for code generation, test design, automation scripting, and documentation.

      • Define governance frameworks for AI-generated test artifacts - validation, review, and sign-off processes to ensure AI outputs meet quality standards.

      • Stay current with AI/ML advancements relevant to testing - intelligent test selection, predictive defect analysis, autonomous test generation, and self-healing automation.

      • Establish metrics to measure the impact of AI adoption on QA velocity, coverage, and defect detection rates.


        • Team Leadership & People Development

        • Lead, mentor, and develop a distributed team of 30+ QA professionals - including QA Leads, Senior QA Engineers, and QA Engineers - across multiple time zones (Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific).

        • Build a high-performance culture rooted in ownership, technical excellence, continuous learning, and psychological safety.

        • Conduct regular 1:1s, career development conversations, and performance reviews. Identify and grow future QA leaders.

        • Design and implement onboarding programs, skill development paths, and technical training curricula - including AI literacy for all QA team members.

        • Manage resource allocation and capacity planning across multiple concurrent projects, ensuring predictable and sustainable QA delivery.

        • Navigate cross-cultural team dynamics with sensitivity and effectiveness - a truly global team requires a global leadership mindset.


          • Process Rigor & Quality Governance

          • Enforce rigorous QA processes across the organization:  • Test case management: Create, maintain, and execute comprehensive test cases in Qase with full traceability (pass, fail, blocked statuses).

          • Bug documentation: Ensure all staging bugs are filed with detailed reproduction steps, expected vs. actual behavior, environment details, screenshots/videos, and severity classification - following established training standards.

          • Automation framework documentation: Maintain clear, up-to-date documentation for all automation frameworks, ensuring any engineer can onboard and contribute.

          • QA Score: Drive iterative improvements in QA Score metrics - tracking automation coverage, defect escape rate, test execution velocity, and regression stability.

            • Define and track QA KPIs and OKRs - present quality dashboards and trend analysis to leadership regularly.

            • Conduct root cause analysis on production escapes and implement systemic corrective actions.


              • Cross-Functional Collaboration

              • Partner closely with Engineering, Product, DevOps, and Release Management to embed quality practices into every phase of the development lifecycle.

              • Work effectively in Agile/Scrum environments - participate in and drive sprint planning, retrospectives, daily stand-ups, and release ceremonies.

              • Act as the primary QA stakeholder for cross-functional initiatives - environment strategy, deployment automation, incident response, and post-mortem processes.

              • Build strong relationships with engineering leadership to ensure QA is not a bottleneck but an accelerator.

                • Common Expectations Across All QA Roles

                • Must be technical and able to write code for testing and automation.

                • Use Claude AI to assist in code creation, automation, and test design.

                • Follow QA processes rigorously: create and execute robust test cases in Qase, maintain clear documentation in automation frameworks, ensure traceability of executed test cases with statuses (pass, fail, blocked), and file Staging Bugs with detailed documentation following training standards.

                • Contribute to iterative improvements in QA Score and testing processes.

                • Strong communication and collaboration skills, analytical mindset, and commitment to continuous learning.

                • Ability to work effectively in Agile/Scrum environments, participating in sprint planning, retrospectives, and daily stand-ups.

• 15+ years of experience in QA/Quality Engineering, with at least 6+ years in Senior Manager or Director-level roles.

  • Proven experience leading teams of 30+ people distributed across multiple time zones and cultural contexts.

    • Hands-on technical proficiency - you can write and review test automation code, not just manage people who do. Proficiency in one or more: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java.

    • Deep expertise in test automation frameworks: Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, or equivalent for UI; REST/GraphQL API testing tools; database validation via SQL.

    • Performance testing experience: K6, JMeter, Gatling, or Locust - designing, executing, and analyzing load/stress/soak tests.

    • Expert knowledge of Git: branching strategies (GitFlow, trunk-based), pull request workflows, code review practices, repository management across multiple repos.

    • Expert knowledge of CI/CD: designing and maintaining pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI), integrating automated tests into build/deploy workflows, debugging pipeline failures.

    • Demonstrated use of AI tools in professional QA work - Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or similar - for test generation, automation coding, defect analysis, or process optimization. Provide specific examples.

    • Strong understanding of Agile/Scrum methodologies and experience operating within and across Agile teams.

    • Experience with test management platforms (Qase, TestRail, Zephyr, or similar).

    • Excellent communication skills - ability to present complex technical quality topics to non-technical stakeholders, write clear documentation, and influence without authority.

    • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent practical experience).

• Experience in the video game, fintech, or e-commerce/payments industry - understanding the unique quality challenges of high-throughput transaction systems.

  • Experience with cloud-native architectures (GCP, AWS, Azure) and testing strategies for microservices, event-driven systems, and distributed architectures.

  • Familiarity with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) for test environment management.

  • Experience building or managing unified test environments - non-production environment strategies that enable safe, deterministic, and scalable validation.

  • Knowledge of security testing fundamentals (OWASP, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning).

  • Experience with data pipeline testing and data quality validation.

  • Background in establishing QA Centers of Excellence or transforming QA organizations from manual-heavy to automation-first.

• 90 days: Complete assessment of current QA processes, tooling, team capabilities, and automation coverage. Establish relationships with all QA leads and key engineering stakeholders. Identify top 3 strategic gaps.

  • 180 days: Deliver a QA strategy roadmap aligned with product and engineering priorities. Implement measurable improvements in automation coverage and CI/CD test integration. Launch AI-assisted testing pilot across at least 2 product teams.

  • 365 days: Achieve measurable reduction in production defect escape rate. Demonstrate >80% automation coverage on critical regression paths. AI-assisted testing practices adopted across all QA teams. QA Score trending consistently upward. Team engagement and retention metrics at or above company benchmarks.

• Lead event strategy, logistics, and on-site execution for Xsolla’s North American and select global events.

  • Support Corporate Events and VIP Events at private venue in Sherman Oaks, CA

  • Manage merchandise inventory, ordering, and allocation for Americas 

  • Manage sponsorship deliverables and partnerships at industry events.

  • Source and negotiate with venues and vendors (booth builders, AV, creative production, hotels, etc.)

  • Maintain and track detailed budgets across multiple currencies and regions.

  • Collaborate with internal marketing teams to develop event-related campaigns, including landing pages, email marketing, and social media initiatives.

  • Create and manage event listings on the Xsolla website and registration platforms (e.g., Splash).

  • Partner with creative teams to brief and deliver event materials, graphics, and branded assets.

  • Coordinate speaking sessions, panel participation, and content development with internal stakeholders.

  • Develop pre-event briefings, on-site run-of-show documents, and post-event reports.

  • Track leads, analytics, and ROI for each event, ensuring timely processing within CRM systems.

  • Support new event research, sponsorship evaluations, and strategic recommendations for future activations.

  • Travel internationally as needed to oversee event delivery and represent Xsolla at global industry gatherings.

• 3+ years of experience in event management or experiential marketing, ideally within the gaming, tech, or software industry.

  • Proven ability to manage global events and understand regional nuances and budgets.

  • Strong project management and organizational skills - able to handle multiple simultaneous projects with precision.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills (written and verbal).

  • Creative problem-solver with the ability to make quick, informed decisions.

  • High attention to detail, quality, and brand alignment.

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace; experience with Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence) is a plus.

  • Familiarity with event registration and marketing platforms such as Splash.

  • Ability to travel internationally and work flexible hours to support global time zones.

1. Field Marketing Strategy

  • 日本市場におけるField Marketing戦略・年間計画の策定

  • Global / APAC Marketing戦略とJapan Business Strategyとの連携

  • ターゲット業界、企業、顧客セグメントに基づいたField Marketing施策の企画

  • Event、Seminar、Webinar、Roundtable、Customer Eventなどのチャネルを組み合わせたIntegrated Campaignの企画

  • Field Marketing活動のKPI設定と継続的な改善

    • 2. Events & Experiences

    • 業界カンファレンス、展示会、セミナー、Networking Eventなどの企画・運営

    • Xsolla主催イベントおよび外部イベントへのスポンサーシップの企画・管理

    • イベントの目的設定、ターゲット設定、コンテンツ企画、集客、当日の運営、Follow-upまでの一貫した管理

    • イベントパートナー、Agency、Vendorとの調整・管理

    • Speaker、Customer、Partnerなどのステークホルダーとの調整

    • イベント後のLead Follow-upおよびSalesとの連携

      • 3. Demand Generation & Pipeline

      • Eventを活用したLead GenerationおよびPipeline Creation

      • Pre-event / During-event / Post-eventのCampaign設計

      • MQL、SQLなどのBusiness KPIのトラッキング

      • イベント参加者を継続的なCustomer Journeyにつなげる施策の設計

        • 4. Content & Thought Leadership

        • イベントやセミナーのテーマ・コンテンツ企画

        • Customer、Partner、Industry Expertとのコンテンツ制作

        • Panel Discussion、Roundtable、Executive Sessionなどの企画

        • 日本のゲーム業界におけるXsollaのThought Leadership強化

        • Global / Regional Contentの日本市場向けローカライズ、翻訳等

          • 5. Customer & Partner Marketing

          • 既存顧客・パートナー向けイベントの企画

          • Customer Success Stories、Case Study、Customer Panelなどの企画

          • Key AccountとのRelationship Buildingを支援するExecutive Eventの企画

          • Strategic Partners、Industry Organizationsとの共同マーケティング

          • Japan Gaming EcosystemにおけるXsollaのNetworkとVisibilityの向上

            • 6. Budget & Vendor Management

            • Field Marketing / Event Budgetの計画・管理

            • Event SponsorshipおよびVendor / Agencyの選定・交渉・管理

            • 予算配分の最適化

            • Global / RegionalのBudget ProcessおよびApproval Processへの対応

              •  

               

              1. Field Marketing Strategy

              • Develop and execute the Field Marketing strategy and annual plan for the Japan market.

              • Align Japan Field Marketing activities with Global / APAC Marketing strategies and Japan business objectives.

              • Plan Field Marketing initiatives based on target industries, companies, and customer segments.

              • Develop integrated campaigns combining events, seminars, webinars, roundtables, customer events, and other channels.

              • Define KPIs for Field Marketing activities and continuously improve performance.

                • 2. Events & Experiences

                • Plan and execute industry conferences, trade shows, seminars, networking events, and other customer-facing experiences.

                • Plan and manage Xsolla-hosted events and external event sponsorships.

                • Manage the entire event lifecycle, including defining objectives and target audiences, content planning, attendee acquisition, on-site execution, and post-event follow-up.

                • Coordinate and manage event partners, agencies, and vendors.

                • Coordinate with key stakeholders, including speakers, customers, and partners.

                • Manage post-event lead follow-up and collaborate closely with Sales.

                  • 3. Demand Generation & Pipeline

                  • Drive lead generation and pipeline creation through event and Field Marketing activities.

                  • Design and execute pre-event, during-event, and post-event campaigns.

                  • Track key business KPIs, including MQLs and SQLs.

                  • Design initiatives that connect event attendees and engagement to an ongoing customer journey.

                    • 4. Content & Thought Leadership

                    • Develop themes and content for events, seminars, and other customer-facing programs.

                    • Create content in collaboration with customers, partners, and industry experts.

                    • Plan and execute panel discussions, roundtables, executive sessions, and other thought leadership programs.

                    • Strengthen Xsolla's thought leadership and visibility within the Japanese gaming industry.

                    • Localize and translate Global / Regional content for the Japanese market.

                      • 5. Customer & Partner Marketing

                      • Plan and execute events and engagement programs for existing customers and partners.

                      • Develop Customer Success Stories, Case Studies, Customer Panels, and other customer-focused initiatives.

                      • Plan executive-level events that support relationship building with key accounts.

                      • Develop joint marketing initiatives with strategic partners and industry organizations.

                      • Strengthen Xsolla's network, visibility, and presence across the Japan gaming ecosystem.

                        • 6. Budget & Vendor Management

                        • Plan and manage the Field Marketing and Event budget.

                        • Select, negotiate with, and manage event sponsors, vendors, and agencies.

                        • Optimize budget allocation based on business priorities and performance.

                        • Manage and comply with Global / Regional budget and approval processes.

応募要件

  • 5年以上のB2B Marketing / Field Marketing / Event Marketing経験

  • Technology、Gaming、SaaS、Platform、FintechなどのB2B企業での経験があることが望ましい

  • カンファレンス、展示会、セミナー、Networking Event、Roundtableなどの企画・運営経験

  • Event / Field MarketingをLead Generationにつなげた経験

  • Marketing Budget、Agency、Vendor、Event Sponsorshipの管理経験

  • 複数のStakeholderを巻き込み、プロジェクトを推進できる高いコミュニケーション能力

  • 戦略立案だけでなく、自ら手を動かして実行できるHands-onな姿勢

    • 言語

    • 日本語：ネイティブレベル
    • 英語：ビジネスレベル以上

      • 求める人物像

      • 自ら考え、主体的に行動できる方
      • 「イベントを開催すること」ではなく、Business Impactを考えてMarketing施策を設計できる方
      • 変化の多い環境でも柔軟に対応できる方
      • 複数のプロジェクトを同時に管理し、優先順位をつけられる方
      • 社内外のさまざまなStakeholderと良好な関係を構築できる方
      • データを見ながら施策を改善できる方
      • 新しいアイデアや方法を積極的に試せる方

        • Qualifications

        • 5+ years of experience in B2B Marketing, Field Marketing, or Event Marketing.

        • Experience in B2B companies within Technology, Gaming, SaaS, Platforms, Fintech, or related industries is preferred.

        • Proven experience planning and executing conferences, trade shows, seminars, networking events, roundtables, and other customer-facing programs.

        • Proven experience leveraging Event / Field Marketing to generate leads and contribute to business growth.

        • Experience managing Marketing Budgets, Agencies, Vendors, and Event Sponsorships.

        • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage multiple stakeholders and drive projects forward.

        • A hands-on mindset, with the ability to not only develop strategies but also execute initiatives independently.

          • Languages

          • Japanese: Native-level proficiency

          • English: Business-level proficiency or above

            • Ideal Candidate Profile

            We are looking for someone who:

            • Thinks independently and takes ownership of their work.

            • Designs marketing initiatives with a clear focus on business impact, rather than simply organizing events.

            • Can adapt flexibly to a fast-changing environment.

            • Can manage multiple projects simultaneously and effectively prioritize tasks.

            • Can build and maintain strong relationships with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.

            • Uses data and performance insights to continuously improve marketing initiatives.

            • Is proactive in testing and adopting new ideas, approaches, and tools.

業界イベント、カンファレンス、セミナー、ウェビナー、ラウンドテーブル、顧客向けイベント、パートナーイベントなど、さまざまなリアル・オンラインのマーケティング施策を通じて、ブランド認知の向上、リード獲得、顧客エンゲージメント、Pipeline創出、Revenue Growthに貢献します。他チームと連携し、ターゲット顧客に適した施策を企画し、実行から効果測定・改善まで一貫して担当します。本ポジションの勤務地は日本・東京です。
 
 
ABOUT US（会社概要）

We are looking for a Field Marketing Manager, Japan to lead the planning and execution of field marketing initiatives that drive brand awareness, customer engagement, lead generation, pipeline creation, and revenue growth in the Japanese market.

• Manage the end-to-end budget and investment approval process, from request intake to closure, and ensure compliance with authorization policies and approval hierarchies.

• Perform financial reconciliations with partners following established procedures and guidelines.
  • Review completed reconciliations to check the accuracy and completeness of results.
  • Assist with analyzing outstanding accounts payable (AP) balances and reviewing AP alerts to identify discrepancies and items requiring further investigation.
  • Audit financial documentation in Box to check report availability, completeness, and compliance with established procedures.
  • Review financial reports and supporting documentation for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Assist with reviewing and updating accounts payable and accounts receivable workflows and process documentation.
  • Maintain and update Finance Operations documentation and procedures in Confluence.
  • Document reconciliation procedures, key learnings, identified discrepancies, and potential process improvements.
  • Support the team with recurring financial operations tasks and other operational activities as required.

• Education: Currently in the final year of a university degree or recently graduated in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a closely related field.
  • Academic Performance: Minimum CGPA of 3.5 for candidates without relevant work experience, or 3.3 for candidates with relevant work experience.
  • English Proficiency: Strong English communication skills (minimum B2). CVs and cover letters must be submitted in English.
  • Analytical Skills: Basic understanding of financial and accounting concepts, with the ability to analyze information, identify inconsistencies, and draw logical conclusions.
  • Attention to Detail: Careful and methodical approach to working with numbers, financial records, and documentation.
  • Technical Skills: Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. Familiarity with formulas, filters, and data organization is an advantage.
  • Problem-Solving: Willingness to investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and learn how to resolve unfamiliar issues.
  • Responsibility and Organization: Ability to manage assigned tasks, follow established procedures, meet deadlines, and maintain accurate records.
  • Learning Mindset: Motivation to develop practical skills in financial operations, learn new tools and systems, and respond constructively to feedback.
  • Working Style: Comfortable performing recurring operational tasks independently after training, while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate issues.
  • Availability: Available for an on-site internship in Kuala Lumpur.

We are seeking a highly analytical and hands-on Senior FinOps Engineer to lead and mature our cloud and infrastructure financial management capabilities across GCP, AWS, and on-prem environments. • Lead the cloud cost optimization strategy across GCP, AWS, and on-prem infrastructure, ensuring efficiency, transparency, and financial predictability
  • Analyze compute, storage, networking, and Kubernetes resource usage to identify actionable cost-saving opportunities without compromising performance or reliability
  • Build and maintain forecasting models, dashboards, and automated reporting that provide real-time visibility into cost drivers and trends across teams and services
  • Develop and implement tagging/labeling standards, budgeting processes, and governance policies to enable cross-organizational accountability
  • Collaborate closely with Engineering, Finance, and Product to guide workload placement, architecture decisions, and scaling strategies
  • Drive adoption of FinOps best practices including rightsizing, reservation planning, autoscaling optimizations, multi-cloud efficiency, and cost-effective storage strategies
  • Create and refine internal tooling, automation, and pipelines for cost monitoring, anomaly detection, and usage attribution across Kubernetes clusters, virtual machines and physical servers, located both in datacenters and cloud providers
  • Advocate for a cost-aware culture by training engineering teams, running FinOps reviews, and communicating insights to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Stay up to date with the latest cloud pricing models, vendor offerings, and industry trends to continuously evolve Xsolla’s FinOps maturity

• 5+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, SRE, or DevOps roles with a strong focus on cost optimization

• Build and evolve scalable, high-performance web applications using React (or Vue) with Next.js for SSR and modern web delivery.
  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, and backend engineers to translate complex monetization workflows into intuitive user experiences.
  • Optimize frontend performance, focusing on loading times, rendering speed, and bundle efficiency, especially in data-heavy dashboards.
  • Ensure cross-browser and multi-device compatibility while meeting accessibility (a11y) and usability standards.
  • Participate in code reviews, share best practices, and help maintain high engineering standards within the frontend team.
  • Work closely with DevOps to streamline CI/CD pipelines, improve deployment reliability, and enhance observability through metrics and monitoring tools.
  • Own features end-to-end requirement refinement, implementation, testing, and delivery.

• 3-5+ years of professional experience in frontend development using React or Vue (React + Next.js preferred).
  • Solid experience with Next.js (SSR, SSG, routing, API routes, caching, and performance optimization).
  • Strong skills in JavaScript (ES6+) and TypeScript, with a good understanding of component architecture and design patterns.
  • Experience with modern tooling (Vite, Webpack, Babel) and UI frameworks (Tailwind CSS, styled-components, Vuetify).
  • Hands-on experience with state management systems (Redux, Vuex, Pinia, Context API, or React Query/SWR).
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, and testing frameworks (Jest, RTL, Vue Test Utils).
  • Strong understanding of performance tuning, responsive design, and cross-platform development.
  • Proficiency in Figma for designing UI/UX layouts, components, and interactive prototypes.
  • Experience with Framer Motion for building high-quality animations and micro-interactions in React applications.
  • Excellent communication skills, proficiency in English for technical discussions and documentation.

• Experience with TypeScript-first environments. Exposure to micro-frontends, edge rendering, or PWAs.
  • Knowledge of animation frameworks (GSAP, Three.js) or advanced motion/interaction design.
  • Background in gaming, fintech, or high-load consumer platforms. Experience with analytics dashboards, virtualization libraries, or complex internal tools.
  • Familiarity feature flagging, AB testing, or Monetization systems.
  • Experience migrating legacy codebases or leading UI modernization projects.

• Build and evolve scalable, high-performance web applications using React and Node.js 
  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, and backend engineers to translate complex requirements into intuitive user experiences.
  • Participate in code reviews, share best practices, and help maintain high engineering standards within the frontend team. Work closely with DevOps to streamline CI/CD pipelines, improve deployment reliability, and enhance observability through metrics and monitoring tools.
  • Own features end-to-end — requirement refinement, implementation, testing, and delivery. Optimize frontend performance, focusing on loading times, rendering speed, and bundle efficiency.
  • Ensure cross-browser and multi-device compatibility while meeting accessibility (a11y) and usability standards.
  • Contribute to  modernization, refactoring, and performance enhancements to keep the platform scalable, maintainable, and aligned with product goals.
  • Contribute and enforce engineering best practices across coding, documentation, testing, and review processes.
  • Ensure strong automated test coverage and reliable CI/CD workflows that reduce manual effort and improve delivery predictability.
  • Own operational excellence, including incident response, root-cause analysis, and long-term reliability improvements.
  • Advocate for scalability, performance, security, and observability across the platform’s architecture and tooling.
  • Identify technical risks, estimate complexity, and communicate trade-offs to leadership and stakeholders.

• 4+ years of software development experience with strong expertise in modern frontend engineering at scale.
  • Deep hands-on knowledge of React including component architecture, SSR patterns, RSC, and complex UI data flows. Proficiency with Node.js and MongoDB for server-side functionality.
  • Strong understanding of modern styling systems and theming approaches (vanilla-extract, styled-components, design tokens).
  • Solid TypeScript practices, including strict typing, shared contracts, and schema validation (Zod or equivalent).
  • Experience with Module Federation.
  • Good understanding of bundling and compilation, experience with webpack/rollup/vite/esbuild
  • Experience with automated testing frameworks (Vitest/Jest) and end-to-end testing (Playwright/Cypress).
  • Good understanding of backend integration patterns (REST, GraphQL, RPC-style APIs).
  • Experience with CI/CD workflows (GitLab CI or similar), private registries, and secure artifact handling.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

• Experience building platforms or tooling used across multiple frontend teams (design systems, template engines, configuration frameworks).
  • Experience with react-native/mobile experience.
  • Knowledge of performance optimization strategies for client-side and server-side rendering.
  • Understanding of accessibility, internationalization, and semantic UI design best practices.
  • Experience developing SDKs, CLI tools, or developer-facing automation.
  • Familiarity with event-driven UI flows, real-time interfaces, or edge-rendering strategies.
  • Background improving developer platforms, observability stacks, or performance monitoring systems.
  • Comfort with UI-as-data approaches and leveraging AI-assisted/no-code tooling to accelerate feature delivery.

lists.content:
First 6 months — priorities in order


- Deal pipeline live: origination intake through credit committee, with the full audit trail. - Scoring data layer: borrower financials and payment telemetry ingested, stored, and under documented data contracts. - LP / fundraising pipeline instrumented, and first investor reporting shipped.
Explicitly out of scope: legal documentation, fund administration, and accounting — these sit with external providers.

Phase 1: Build (through first close)

Deal pipeline management
- Design and run the full deal workflow: origination intake, screening, scoring, credit committee, closing.
- Implement it as governed automation (workflow orchestration such as n8n or similar, with LLM-assisted steps where they add value): every automated output validated against a defined schema, low-confidence results routed to human review, and a complete audit trail suitable for LP due diligence.

Scoring and underwriting data layer
- Build the ingestion and storage layer for borrower financials and payments telemetry (including Xsolla transaction data) — PostgreSQL or equivalent, ETL pipelines, materialized views, documented data contracts.
- Develop credit scoring and forecasting models in Python, with proper train/test discipline, leakage and PII exclusion, and ongoing monitoring for drift and degradation.
- Maintain evaluation and regression checks so model and automation quality is measured continuously, not assumed.

Fundraising / LP pipeline
- Build and operate the investor pipeline: CRM automation, conference and referral pipeline tracking, follow-up orchestration, and data room preparation and upkeep.
- Instrument the pipeline so we always know conversion rates, stage aging, and next actions per LP.

Investor and borrower dashboards
- Ship reporting for both audiences: fund-level metrics for investors, facility-level metrics for borrowers.
- Numbers must reconcile to source systems and be reproducible outside the BI tool — audit-grade, not demo-grade. Tableau / Power BI or a lightweight web dashboard, whichever fits.

Reliability, cost, and security of the stack
- Budget caps and cost monitoring on all AI-assisted automation; regression canaries before changes ship.
- Access control and data protection appropriate for fund data: deny-by-default permissions, audit logs, strict handling of LP identities, borrower financials, and deal terms. 
- Documented runbooks and handover-ready documentation as part of "done" — the stack must be operable by someone other than its author.

Phase 2: Operate (post-close)

- Move into an operating role on the underwriting side: portfolio monitoring, covenant and collateral tracking, scenario and stress analysis.
- Extend the platform to other investment types and support the capital formation team with the same pipeline and reporting infrastructure.

Client and investor facing
This is not a back-office role. The person will join investor and borrower meetings, present the dashboards and the numbers behind them, and field diligence questions directly. Fluency in finance conversations is as important as engineering. The person will also respond to LP operational due diligence questionnaires on the data and automation stack.

Required

- 7+ years across data analytics / data engineering, including recent hands-on experience building and running production automation (not prototypes or notebooks).

- Proven production experience with LLM-based automation: schema-validated outputs, human review gates, evaluation and regression testing, cost-tiered model routing.

- Strong SQL and Python; ownership of a PostgreSQL (or similar) data platform end to end — ETL, materialized views, performance tuning, data contracts.

- Workflow orchestration experience (n8n, Airflow, or comparable).

- BI and dashboarding: Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, or equivalent web dashboards; a track record of reporting that executives actually used for decisions.

- Security discipline for sensitive data: role-based access, deny-by-default policies, audit trails, PII handling.

- Finance background: degree in finance or quantitative field plus real experience in portfolio analytics, market risk, or credit — able to hold their own in an underwriting or investor conversation.

- Strong written and spoken English; comfortable presenting to senior external audiences.

Preferred

- Direct exposure to private credit, lending, or fund operations.

- Forecasting and statistical modeling track record (capacity planning, SLA/risk forecasting, or similar).

- Experience with embeddings / semantic search and multi-model AI setups.

- Web development ability (React / TypeScript or similar) for internal tools and dashboards.

- Experience in audited or regulated environments (SOC 2, fund audits, or equivalent).

ABOUT US 
Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. Beyond its core commerce platform, Xsolla is building a private credit fund that lends to video game studios, underwritten with a data advantage no traditional lender has: Xsolla's own payments telemetry across thousands of games. The fund is in its capital formation phase and is led by Stan Rudoi, Chief Credit Officer. This is a ground-floor opportunity to help raise a first-time fund inside a profitable, global gaming-commerce company, alongside the broader Xsolla capital markets ecosystem (Xsolla Funding Club, Xsolla SPAC 1 — Nasdaq: XSLLU, and other strategic vehicles).
For more information, visit xsolla.com.

lists.content:
Fund Formation and Structuring

  • Drive fund formation with external fund counsel: vehicle and jurisdiction selection, LPA and side letters, GP and management company setup, and the regulatory perimeter.
  • Own the LPA from the operator's seat: terms, economics, and governance mechanics — and translate them into operational reality once signed.

    • Service Provider Stack

  • Select and manage the provider stack: fund administrator, auditor, tax advisors, banking/custody, and compliance vendors — and manage them to institutional standards.
  • Own provider economics: negotiate scopes and fees; keep the fund's operating cost model lean and LP-defensible.

    • Fund Operations

  • Run the core machinery: capital calls and distributions, LP onboarding and KYC/AML, expense management, and cash movement controls.
  • Own valuation and NAV: valuation policy, NAV oversight with the administrator, and credit-fund specifics such as borrowing-base mechanics and leverage facility administration.

    • LP Reporting and Diligence Readiness

  • Build the reporting stack: quarterly reporting (ILPA-aligned), capital account statements, and LP communications infrastructure.
  • Keep the fund diligence-ready: DDQ responses, operational due-diligence readiness, and the operations sections of the data room — before LPs ask.

    • Compliance and Governance

  • Establish the policy framework: valuation, allocation, conflicts, and ESG/AML policies; regulatory filings with counsel; audit coordination.
  • Design for scrutiny: so every process has a documented owner, control, and audit trail that stands up to institutional operational due diligence.

    • Operating Playbook and Team Building

  • Codify the fund's operating playbook: documented processes, controls, and owners for every core workflow — built for operational due diligence from day one.
  • Scale the function: as the fund scales, build out and mentor the junior operations team (controller, fund accountants) and integrate with Xsolla's finance and legal teams.

Experience

  • 7+ years in fund operations, fund CFO, or fund controllership roles at private credit or other private capital funds.
  • You have taken at least one private fund from formation through first close — this is the core requirement. You know what breaks, in what order, and how to prevent it.
  • Deep working knowledge of LPA terms, fund administration, capital call mechanics, and ILPA reporting standards.
  • Credit-fund specifics — leverage facilities, borrowing bases, loan administration, asset-level reporting — are a strong plus.

    • Skills and Competencies

  • Hands-on operator: comfortable being the entire operations function on day one, with providers as your leverage.
  • Rigorous documentation and controls discipline; you build processes that pass operational due diligence, not just processes that work.
  • Strong commercial judgment on provider selection, fee negotiation, and build-vs-outsource decisions.
  • Clear communicator who can explain fund mechanics to non-fund people — including investors, borrowers, and Xsolla leadership.

    • Education and Credentials

  • A bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field; CPA, a CFA charter, or an MBA is preferred.

About Xsolla
Xsolla is a global commerce and financial technology company for the video game industry. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices and operations worldwide, Xsolla provides the tools, infrastructure and capital solutions that help developers and publishers fund, launch, distribute and monetize their games across every market and platform. The company serves thousands of game businesses globally, from independent studios to the largest publishers, and is expanding a dedicated capital markets and investment platform serving the interactive entertainment ecosystem.
The Capital Markets Group
The Capital Markets Group (CMG) sits within Xsolla's Global Strategic Initiatives function and operates as the firm's institutional capital platform. The group originates, structures and executes financing and investment solutions across games and interactive entertainment, and is building a franchise modeled on the leading independent capital markets and special situations advisory platforms.
The group operates multiple investment vehicles spanning debt financing and credit markets, alongside special situations and principal investment strategies serving the interactive entertainment ecosystem. These activities are supported by a proprietary market intelligence system, a global events and convening program, and a governed institutional relationship platform covering LPs, sovereign investors, family offices, banks and intermediaries across the Americas, MENA, APAC and Europe.
CMG operates from hubs in Los Angeles, New York, the Middle East and Singapore. The group is in its foundation stage: hires at every level join a live deal environment with executive sponsorship, meaningful ownership and the mandate to build a durable franchise rather than inherit one.
For more information, visit xsolla.com.

About the Opportunity

Xsolla is seeking a Head of Investor Capital and Relations to build the firm's Asia Pacific capital franchise from Singapore. The region combines the world's deepest gaming markets with some of its most sophisticated institutional capital, and this seat exists to connect the two for the firm: sovereign and state linked investors in Singapore, institutional investors and strategics across Korea and Japan, capital markets counterparties in Hong Kong and Australia, and the regional family office community.

The corporate title for this seat is Director, with a defined path to Executive Director tied to franchise milestones, including the 2027 regional coverage plan and team build. There are no direct reports initially; regional analyst support and a 2027 hiring plan are owned by this seat.

The Head of Investor Capital and Relations, APAC will be based in Singapore, in office, leveraging Xsolla's existing APAC presence, and will report to the Senior Vice President of Global Strategic Initiatives and Partnerships. The role requires travel of approximately 40 to 50 percent across Southeast Asia, North Asia and Australia, with periodic travel to Los Angeles. This is a full time position; Employment Pass sponsorship is available, with the package structured with local counsel.

Expressions of Interest

Xsolla welcomes confidential conversations with qualified candidates and trusted introductions. Please direct expressions of interest, together with a resume and a short note on relevant experience, to the Xsolla Talent Acquisition team via the application button linked below.

Role Overview

As Head of Investor Capital and Relations, APAC, you will own senior institutional coverage across the region, spanning sovereign and state linked investors, pensions, insurers, asset managers, funds of funds and family offices, alongside gaming, technology and media strategics across Korea, Japan and Greater China. You will own the coverage map, the relationships and the regional plan, operating with a global reporting line and the support of the firm's existing APAC operating footprint.

This is a builder's role. You will establish the coverage standards, relationship infrastructure and regional plan that allow Xsolla to engage APAC's institutional capital with discipline, while coordinating closely with counsel on marketing approach and applicable regulatory regimes across Singapore, Hong Kong, Korea, Japan and Australia.

Key Responsibilities

Institutional and Strategic Coverage

  • Own institutional coverage. Own senior coverage of APAC institutional capital, including sovereign and state linked investors, pensions and insurers, asset managers, funds of funds and regional family offices, with complete, current records and documented access paths in the firm's relationship platform.

  • Build strategic coverage. Build dedicated coverage of gaming, technology and media strategics across Korea, Japan and Greater China as limited partners, co-investors and transaction counterparties.

  • Map the counterparties. Map each priority institution's decision architecture, including mandate criteria, allocation cadence, co-investment appetite and approval process, and maintain that intelligence as a living asset.

    • Capital Formation and Transactions

    • Lead regional fundraising. Lead regional pre-marketing and fundraising support for the firm's investment vehicles within each jurisdiction's private placement and offering regimes, coordinating with counsel on the marketing approach for Singapore, Hong Kong, Korea, Japan and Australia.

    • Own diligence processes. Originate and manage institutional diligence processes end to end, including DDQ coordination, data room support and operational due diligence visits.

    • Support transactions. Support cross border financing and strategic transaction conversations alongside the Americas and MENA coverage teams and fund principals.

      • Franchise and Regional Platform

      • Build the region's presence. Build the firm's presence across the region's priority investment and gaming industry forums; run the APAC events calendar and convert presence into qualified pipeline.

      • Develop the regional plan. Develop the 2027 regional coverage plan, including market prioritization, any additional country coverage and the regional hiring sequence, for approval by the Group Head.

      • Set coverage standards. Establish coverage and CRM standards for the region and enforce the group's interaction logging discipline.

        • Risk and Controls

        • Ensure regulatory compliance. Ensure all regional marketing and offering activity complies with applicable regimes and the firm's policies, in coordination with counsel, including Singapore's frameworks for fund offers to institutional and accredited investors.

        • Maintain counterparty awareness. Maintain rigorous counterparty awareness, including KYC, AML and sanctions screening coordination, and escalate reputational risk considerations early.

Candidate Profile

Experience

  • 8 or more years of progressive experience in APAC institutional coverage, capital formation, investment banking or investor relations at a bank, asset manager, placement agent or sovereign investor, including significant client facing responsibility.

  • Demonstrable relationships across Singapore's institutional community and at least one of the Korean, Japanese or Greater China institutional or strategic investor markets, with a referenceable record of capital raised or partnerships executed.

  • Sector experience across gaming, interactive entertainment, technology or media, or coverage of strategics in those sectors, is a clear advantage.

    • Domain Expertise

    • Working knowledge of regional fund marketing and private placement practice, including Singapore's institutional and accredited investor frameworks.

    • Experience marketing alternative strategies such as credit, special situations or private equity to Asian institutions is preferred.

    • Experience operating under the Monetary Authority of Singapore regulatory framework, including holding or having held representative status with a capital markets services license holder or operating within an applicable exemption, is preferred.

      • Skills and Competencies

      • Proven ability to operate independently on a global platform, with disciplined pipeline management, reporting and follow through across time zones.

      • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English; professional fluency in Mandarin, Japanese or Korean is preferred.

      • A high degree of ethics and integrity, with a clean regulatory and disciplinary history.

        • Education and Credentials

        • A bachelor's degree is required.

        • A CFA or CAIA charter, or equivalent, is strongly preferred.

About You
As Head of Investor Capital and Relations, Middle East, you will operate independently in region with a global reporting line and executive sponsorship, and with the mandate to build the firm's Middle East franchise from first principles: the coverage map, the institutional relationships, the office and, ultimately, the regional team.
This is a builder's role. You will own senior coverage of the region's sovereign wealth funds, government related entities and family offices, lead the office establishment and hub determination between DIFC and ADGM, and coordinate closely with counsel and the firm's government relations workstreams as you build a durable Gulf franchise.
 
About the Opportunity
Xsolla is seeking a Head of Investor Capital and Relations to be the firm's senior presence in the Gulf and own its most strategically important capital relationships: the region's sovereign wealth funds, government related entities and principal family offices. The GCC is executing one of the most ambitious government backed investment programs in the history of the games industry, and this seat exists to convert that alignment into anchor limited partner relationships, co-investment partnerships and strategic financings for the firm's investment vehicles and transaction pipeline.

lists.content:
Key Responsibilities

Sovereign and Institutional Coverage

  • Own sovereign coverage. Own senior coverage of the region's sovereign wealth funds and government related entities, including their gaming, technology and entertainment investment vehicles, with documented access paths and personal ownership of the firm's most senior regional relationships.

  • Build family office coverage. Build and maintain coverage of the GCC's principal single and multi family offices, regional institutional investors and banks, with complete, current records in the firm's relationship platform.

  • Map the counterparties. Map the decision making architecture of each priority institution, including investment committee cadence, mandate criteria, co-investment appetite and approval chains, and maintain that intelligence as a living asset.

    • Capital Formation and Transactions

    • Lead regional fundraising. Lead regional pre-marketing and fundraising processes for the firm's investment vehicles within applicable private placement and promotion regimes, coordinating with counsel on the marketing approach for each jurisdiction.

    • Originate co-investment dialogues. Originate and manage sovereign co-investment dialogues alongside fund principals, and support strategic and government aligned financing conversations through to execution.

    • Own diligence processes. Manage institutional diligence processes end to end, including DDQ coordination, data room support, operational due diligence visits and reference management.

      • Franchise and Regional Platform

      • Advise on the hub decision. Advise the hub determination between DIFC and ADGM, and lead the establishment of the regional office with Legal and Finance, including regulatory positioning of the firm's regional activities.

      • Build the region's presence. Build the firm's presence across the region's priority investment forums and convening platforms, and run a regional events calendar that converts presence into qualified pipeline.

      • Coordinate with government relations. Coordinate deliberately with the firm's government relations and sovereign engagement workstreams so that capital coverage and institutional diplomacy reinforce one another.

      • Build the regional team. Recruit and develop the regional Relationship Manager and subsequent hires; establish coverage and CRM standards for the region.

        • Risk and Controls

        • Ensure regulatory compliance. Ensure all regional marketing and promotion activity complies with applicable regimes, including DIFC and ADGM promotion rules and the private placement frameworks of each GCC jurisdiction, in coordination with counsel.

        • Maintain counterparty awareness. Maintain rigorous counterparty awareness, including KYC, AML and sanctions screening coordination with the firm's compliance processes, and escalate reputational risk considerations early.

Candidate Profile

Experience

  • 10 or more years covering MENA institutional capital from an investment bank, sovereign investor, placement agent, asset manager or family office platform, including at least 5 years in a senior client facing capacity.

  • Demonstrable senior relationships inside GCC sovereign institutions and principal family offices, with a referenceable record of capital raised, commitments secured or strategic partnerships executed in the region.

  • Existing relationships across the region's sovereign gaming, esports and digital entertainment programs and their investment arms are a strong advantage, as is a cumulative placement or capital formation record in the region of USD 500 million or more.

    • Domain Expertise

    • Working knowledge of the regional regulatory landscape relevant to fund marketing and promotion, including the DIFC and ADGM frameworks and private placement practice across the GCC.

    • Experience marketing alternative strategies such as credit, special situations or private equity to sovereign and family office investors, including familiarity with Shariah aware structuring considerations, is preferred.

    • Experience establishing or operating a regulated or exempt presence in the DIFC or ADGM is preferred.

      • Skills and Competencies

      • Deep cultural fluency and protocol judgment in sovereign, government and family office settings, and the discretion those relationships demand.

      • Proven ability to operate independently in region on a global platform, with disciplined reporting, pipeline management and follow through.

      • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English; Arabic language fluency is preferred.

      • A high degree of ethics and integrity, with a clean regulatory and disciplinary history.

        • Education and Credentials

        • A bachelor's degree is required.

        • A CFA or CAIA charter, or equivalent, is preferred.

About Xsolla
Xsolla is a global video game commerce company that provides the tools and infrastructure the gaming industry relies on to build, distribute, and monetize games. Working with developers and publishers of every size, from independent studios to the largest franchises in the world, Xsolla operates as a merchant of record and processes payments across more than 200 countries and territories, supporting over 1,000 payment methods, 130 currencies, and 25 languages. Its platform spans the full game lifecycle, including web shops, Pay Station, Login, Launcher, the In-Game Store, and a broad suite of LiveOps and monetization tools.
Strategic Initiatives and Capital Markets
Beyond its core commerce platform, Xsolla has built an expanding set of strategic and capital markets initiatives. The company connects developers with capital through programs such as the Xsolla Funding Club, and it has extended its footprint into the public markets through Xsolla SPAC 1 (Nasdaq: XSLLU), a publicly listed acquisition vehicle focused on gaming, fintech, adtech, and related technology sectors. These activities sit alongside a growing portfolio of partnerships, market expansion programs, and new business lines led by the Global Strategic Initiatives and Partnerships organization.
Market Opportunity
The opportunity is significant. The global games market is on track to exceed 300 billion dollars, and the sector has matured into a genuine institutional asset class. Industry trackers recorded roughly 161 billion dollars of games industry mergers and acquisitions in , and private equity firms, strategic acquirers, and sovereign investors continue to deploy capital into the studios, platforms, and infrastructure that power the industry. Xsolla sits at the center of this commerce layer, which positions the company to play a meaningful role in how capital flows through gaming.
For more information, visit xsolla.com.

About the Opportunity

Xsolla is seeking a Head of Investor Capital and Relations to lead its capital formation and investor relations agenda from New York. This senior, high-visibility mandate brings together two disciplines that are often treated separately: raising and structuring capital, and stewarding the relationships and narrative that sustain long-term investor confidence. The successful candidate will own the institutional capital relationships that support Xsolla’s strategic vehicles and initiatives and serve as a principal point of contact between the company and the global investment community.

The role reports directly to the Senior Vice President of Global Strategic Initiatives and Partnerships and works in close partnership with the Chief Executive, Chief Legal Officer, finance leadership, and the founders. It is designed for an investor who understands capital from the inside: someone who has sat across the table from sponsors, sovereign funds, and institutional allocators, and who can translate Xsolla’s strategy into a compelling, credible investment thesis.

The Head of Investor Capital and Relations will be based in New York and will report to Rytis Joseph Jan, Senior Vice President of Global Strategic Initiatives and Partnerships. The role requires significant global travel, including regular engagement across the Gulf, Asia, and major financial centers, to build and maintain the relationships at the heart of the mandate.

Expressions of Interest

Xsolla welcomes confidential conversations with qualified candidates and trusted introductions. Please direct expressions of interest, together with a resume and a short note on relevant experience, to the Xsolla Talent Acquisition team via the application button linked below.

Role Overview

As Head of Investor Capital and Relations, you will be responsible for the full arc of capital engagement, from sourcing and cultivating investors, to structuring and executing capital raises, to maintaining disciplined, compliant, and trusted relationships once capital is committed. Your remit will span private capital formation, sovereign and strategic institutional relationships, and the investor relations function associated with Xsolla's publicly listed activities.

You will build the investor relations capability that a company operating in and around the public markets requires, including the disclosure discipline, messaging consistency, and relationship infrastructure that institutional investors expect. You will also act as a senior commercial partner to the deal teams, helping to shape the capital structure, investor syndicate, and positioning of strategic transactions.

This is a builder's role. You will establish the processes, materials, and team that allow Xsolla to engage the capital markets with the professionalism of a far larger institution, while retaining the speed and ambition of a company in a high growth sector.

Key Responsibilities

Capital Formation and Fundraising

  • Lead capital raises. Design and execute capital raises across the firm's strategic vehicles and initiatives, spanning equity, structured, and credit instruments.

  • Own the investor pipeline. Develop and manage the investor pipeline, from initial sourcing and qualification through diligence, negotiation, and close.

  • Build the materials. Create the core fundraising materials, including the equity story, investor presentations, data rooms, and the supporting financial narrative, in partnership with finance and legal.

  • Structure terms. Shape terms and commitments in coordination with deal leadership, balancing the interests of the firm, its founders, and incoming investors.

  • Read the market. Maintain a current and accurate view of market conditions, investor appetite, and comparable transactions to inform timing and structure.

    • Sovereign Wealth and Strategic Institutional Capital

    Gulf sovereign wealth funds alone manage on the order of 5 trillion dollars in assets and have become active, thematic investors in technology and platform businesses, with leading funds such as QIA, PIF, ADIA, Mubadala, and ADQ frequently writing large strategic commitments. Cultivating and stewarding these relationships is central to this role.

    • Originate relationships. Build and steward relationships with sovereign wealth funds, strategic corporates, family offices, and large institutional allocators, with particular emphasis on the Gulf, Asia, and North America.

    • Map the counterparties. Understand the priorities, mandates, and decision processes of target institutions, and align Xsolla's opportunities to the right counterparties and ticket sizes.

    • Engage principals. Serve as a trusted, senior relationship owner who can engage principals and investment committees with credibility and discretion.

    • Coordinate coverage. Align coverage strategy with banking partners and advisors to maximize reach into the institutions that matter most.

      • Public Markets, SPAC, and Business Combination Investor Relations

      • Build the IR function. Establish and run the investor relations function for Xsolla's publicly listed activities, including Xsolla SPAC 1, in line with the standards expected of a public company.

      • Manage public investors. Manage relationships with public market investors, sell side and buy side analysts, and prospective shareholders, and serve as a primary point of contact for inbound investor inquiries.

      • Lead event communications. Lead investor communications around capital events, including any business combination, and prepare leadership for investor meetings, roadshows, and earnings style updates.

      • Craft the message. Develop consistent, accurate messaging that links strategy, key metrics, and results, and that supports informed engagement and durable investor confidence.

      • Protect disclosure integrity. Partner with legal and compliance to uphold disclosure obligations, including fair disclosure principles, blackout periods, and safe harbor language for forward looking statements.

        • Capital Markets Strategy and Transaction Execution

        • Advise on structure. Advise leadership on capital structure, funding strategy, and the optimal mix of capital across the firm's objectives.

        • Support transactions. Support the execution of strategic transactions, including acquisitions and business combinations, by shaping the investor syndicate, terms, and positioning.

        • Coordinate advisors. Direct the work of banks, advisors, and counsel through diligence and execution, and keep workstreams aligned to timeline and outcome.

        • Translate the market. Monitor capital markets developments, sector valuations, and competitor activity, and translate them into recommendations for leadership and, where relevant, the board.

          • Disclosure, Communications, and Governance

          • Set the framework. Establish and maintain a disciplined disclosure and communications framework, including policies, calendars, and approval workflows.

          • Prepare materials. Prepare board level and investor level materials, and contribute to the narrative that the company presents to the market.

          • Ensure compliance. Ensure that all investor facing communications are accurate, consistent, and compliant, and that material information is handled appropriately.

            • Leadership and Cross-Functional Partnership

            • Build the team. Recruit, mentor, and lead the investor relations and capital markets team over time.

            • Work across the firm. Partner seamlessly across finance, legal, strategy, communications, and the founders to deliver a unified message to the market.

            • Represent Xsolla. Represent the company with poise and authority at investor meetings, industry forums, and capital markets events around the world.

              •

Candidate Profile

Experience

  • Twelve to fifteen years or more of progressive experience across investment banking, private equity, sovereign wealth or institutional investing, capital markets, or senior investor relations, ideally spanning more than one of these.

  • A demonstrable track record of raising or deploying institutional capital and of closing complex transactions.

  • Direct experience engaging sovereign wealth funds, strategic investors, or large institutional allocators at a senior level.

  • Exposure to public company investor relations, the listing process, or a business combination is strongly preferred.

    • Domain Expertise

    • Deep fluency in capital structure, private placements, equity and credit instruments, and transaction processes.

    • A strong working knowledge of public market disclosure, fair disclosure principles, and the obligations that accompany a listing.

    • Familiarity with gaming, technology, fintech, or other high growth sectors is a clear advantage, as is comfort operating across the Gulf, Asia, and North American markets.

      • Skills and Competencies

      • Exceptional financial acumen, with the ability to build and interrogate the analysis behind a capital raise.

      • Outstanding written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn a complex strategy into a clear and persuasive investment narrative.

      • Significant relationship capital and the gravitas to engage principals, investment committees, and senior executives.

      • Sound judgment, discretion, and the highest standards of integrity when handling sensitive and material information.

      • The drive and resourcefulness to build a function from the ground up in a fast moving environment.

        • Education and Credentials

        • A bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, or a related field is required.

        • An advanced degree such as an MBA, or a professional credential such as the CFA, is strongly preferred.

        • Relevant securities licenses, or the willingness to obtain them, are viewed favorably.

Working with developers and publishers of every size, from independent studios to the largest franchises in the world, Xsolla operates as a merchant of record and processes payments across more than 200 countries and territories, supporting over 1,000 payment methods, 130 currencies, and 25 languages. Its platform spans the full game lifecycle, including web shops, Pay Station, Login, Launcher, the In-Game Store, and a broad suite of LiveOps and monetization tools.
Strategic Initiatives and Capital Markets
Beyond its core commerce platform, Xsolla has built an expanding set of strategic and capital markets initiatives. The company connects developers with capital through programs such as the Xsolla Funding Club, and it has extended its footprint into the public markets through Xsolla SPAC 1 (Nasdaq: XSLLU), a publicly listed acquisition vehicle focused on gaming, fintech, adtech, and related technology sectors. These activities sit alongside a growing portfolio of partnerships, market expansion programs, and new business lines led by the Global Strategic Initiatives and Partnerships organization.
Market Opportunity
The opportunity is significant. The global games market is on track to exceed 300 billion dollars, and the sector has matured into a genuine institutional asset class. Industry trackers recorded roughly 161 billion dollars of games industry mergers and acquisitions in , and private equity firms, strategic acquirers, and sovereign investors continue to deploy capital into the studios, platforms, and infrastructure that power the industry. Xsolla sits at the center of this commerce layer, which positions the company to play a meaningful role in how capital flows through gaming.
For more information, visit xsolla.com.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
 
Xsolla is seeking a Head of Investor Relations for the Xsolla Credit Fund, whose primary mandate is LP capital raising. While Xsolla's Capital Markets team covers investor relations across all of the company's strategic vehicles, this role is dedicated to the credit fund. Over time the role will also support fundraising for other Xsolla investment products, but the credit fund remains the primary focus.This is a relationship-led role. We are looking for someone who brings an established network of LP relationships — family offices, credit and alternatives allocators, funds of funds, and institutions — and who can open doors, engage principals, and personally steward investors from first conversation through diligence to commitment.
ABOUT US 
Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game.
Beyond its core commerce platform, Xsolla is building a private credit fund that lends to video game studios and gaming businesses, underwritten with a data advantage no traditional lender has: Xsolla's own payments telemetry across thousands of games. The fund is in its capital formation phase and is led by Stan Rudoi, Chief Credit Officer. This is a ground-floor opportunity to help raise a first-time fund inside a profitable, global gaming-commerce company, alongside the broader Xsolla capital markets ecosystem (Xsolla Funding Club, Xsolla SPAC 1 — Nasdaq: XSLLU, and other strategic vehicles).
For more information, visit xsolla.com.

lists.content:
LP Relationships and Origination

  • Bring and grow the network: activate your existing LP relationships and originate new ones across family offices, credit and alternatives allocators, funds of funds, and institutions.
  • Engage principals: represent the fund credibly with decision-makers and investment committees, and match opportunities to each investor's mandate and ticket size.
  • Source and qualify the wider funnel: from conferences, investor databases, introductions, Xsolla contacts, and external research — qualified and prioritized by mandate fit.
  • Steward each relationship through diligence, negotiation, and commitment — and after the close, as the foundation of the fund's long-term LP base.

    • Follow-Through and Pipeline Discipline

  • Drive follow-through from first contact to meeting, diligence, soft interest, and closed commitment — no lead goes stale.
  • Prepare and send investor outreach and follow-ups; capture meeting notes, next steps, and commitment tracking after every interaction.
  • Maintain clean CRM reporting: pipeline status, activity, outcomes, blockers, priorities, and weekly progress — so leadership always knows conversion rates, stage aging, and next actions per LP.
  • Provide regular internal fund progress reporting to Xsolla leadership via Slack and other internal tools. A junior IR hire will take on pipeline operations as the raise scales.

    • Fundraising Materials and Messaging

  • Support and continuously improve investor materials: pitch deck, FAQs, data room, and meeting-specific talking points.
  • Refine LP messaging, fund thesis, objection handling, and investor segmentation based on live market feedback.
  • Write concise, institutional-quality investor emails, follow-ups, and presentation language.

    • Diligence and Fund Setup Support

  • Coordinate LP diligence requests across internal Xsolla teams, external advisors, legal, finance, and leadership.
  • Support fund setup workstreams: data room preparation and upkeep, reporting readiness, and document management.
  • Collect and synthesize investor feedback on fund terms, structure, risk-return profile, reporting, and allocation preferences to inform fund design.

    • Cross-Product Fundraising Support

  • As capacity allows, extend the same funnel discipline and materials support to other Xsolla investment products and strategic vehicles, in coordination with the Capital Markets team.

Experience

  • 7+ years in investor relations, placement, private funds, investment banking, private credit, venture capital, private equity, family office, or institutional fundraising.
  • An established, referenceable network of LP relationships — family offices, credit and alternatives allocators, funds of funds, or institutions — that you can activate for a first-time fund. This is the core requirement for the role.
  • A track record of raising institutional capital, with a strong understanding of LP fundraising mechanics: fund materials, diligence processes, investor segmentation, and the private fund lifecycle.
  • Direct exposure to private credit or first-time fund raises is a strong plus.

    • Skills and Competencies

  • Excellent business English; able to write concise investor emails, follow-ups, FAQs, and presentation language without supervision.
  • Strong Excel / Google Sheets, CRM, tracking, reporting, and project management discipline.
  • Commercial, structured, responsive, and able to manage many parallel investor conversations without dropping threads.
  • The gravitas and credibility to engage principals, investment committees, and senior allocators as a peer.
  • Sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive fund and investor information.
  • Interest in gaming, fintech, private credit, alternative investments, or digital platforms preferred.

    • Education and Credentials

  • A bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, or a related field is preferred.
  • CFA / CAIA or relevant securities licenses are viewed favorably but not required.

lists.content:
Underwriting Framework and Credit Policy

  • Design the fund's underwriting framework from scratch: credit policy, underwriting standards, rating and scoring methodology, credit memo templates, and approval workflows — built for LP diligence from day one.
  • Build the data edge into the process: integrate Xsolla's payments telemetry and game-revenue data into underwriting as a durable information advantage.

    • Deal Underwriting and Structuring

  • Lead the underwriting of lending facilities to game studios and gaming businesses: financial analysis, revenue durability, downside cases, and recovery analysis.
  • Structure facilities: term loans, revolvers, royalty- and revenue-based structures — including covenants, collateral packages, borrowing bases, and pricing.
  • Draft and negotiate term sheets and credit documentation with borrowers alongside external counsel.

    • Credit Committee and Governance

  • Stand up and run the credit committee process: present transactions, document decisions, and maintain an audit trail that stands up to LP and auditor scrutiny.
  • Establish portfolio monitoring: watchlist discipline, covenant tracking, and a workout playbook as the portfolio builds.

    • LP Diligence and Fundraising Support

  • Be the credit face of the fund: appear in fund materials and LP meetings as the fund's credit authority; own underwriting answers in LP due diligence.
  • Support capital formation: help shape the fund's risk-return narrative, portfolio construction guidelines, and track-record presentation.

    • Credit Playbook and Team Building

  • Codify the credit playbook: standards, templates, and documentation that make the fund's underwriting repeatable and audit-ready.
  • Build the bench: as the fund scales, hire and mentor the junior credit team — analysts, associates, and in time a portfolio/risk officer.

Experience

  • 7+ years in private credit, direct lending, specialty finance, or leveraged finance, with personal responsibility for underwriting and closing institutional credit transactions.
  • Experience at an early-stage or first-time credit fund — credit policy written from scratch, LPA input, first LP diligence — is strongly preferred. You have seen what a fund needs before it has infrastructure.
  • Lending against media, IP, royalties, recurring digital revenue, or gaming businesses is a strong plus.
  • A track record you can walk LPs through: deals underwritten, structures used, and how they performed — including the ones that went wrong and what you did about it.

    • Skills and Competencies

  • Deep fluency in credit analysis, financial modeling, covenant design, collateral structures, and credit documentation.
  • The gravitas to sit across from LPs, investment committees, and founders — and the judgment to say no to a deal.
  • Enjoys mentoring junior team members and building a strong credit culture as the team grows.
  • Comfort operating in a lean, fast-moving team where you build the machine you then operate.

    • Education and Credentials

  • A bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, or a related field; an MBA and/or a CFA charter is preferred.
